entries.bounds_rationale: Denominator of the afterbody branch of cfr-25-appB-fig2-k1 and -k2.
entries.definition: Distance from the main step to the stern post. Carries the hull at low speed and in the stern landing case, and its ventilation behind the step is what stops the hull sticking to the water on takeoff.

measurement_convention.datum: From the main step, parallel to the hull reference axis.
measurement_convention.notes: 25.529(a)(3) applies the stern landing load at 85 percent of this length, not at its end, so the station where the load acts and the station where the figure reads K1 = 1.0 are not the same place.
measurement_convention.source: 14 CFR Part 25, Appendix B, figure 2 (image EC28SE91.056)
measurement_convention.station: Terminates at the stern post.

verification.checked_against: Appendix B figure 2, read from the published image, eCFR issue 2026-07-07.

entries.bounds_rationale: Denominator of every Stevens-series coefficient, as b^3 in the load and resistance coefficients.
entries.definition: The beam of the hull at the main step. The characteristic dimension of the Stevens Institute tank series: every coefficient in NACA ARR 4F15 divides by it.

measurement_convention.datum: Transverse, in the section at the main step, over the chines, excluding spray strips. The source does not say what the beam is taken over; the over-chines convention is DEFINED HERE, as for maximum-beam.
measurement_convention.notes: Where a hull's chine planform is widest at the step, this equals maximum-beam. ARR L5G23 Table I files the Stevens series' 5.40 inches under "Maximum beam", which is right only if those hulls are widest at the step; no source read says they are.
measurement_convention.source: NACA ARR 4F15, p. 11: "b beam at main step, feet", in the definitions of C_delta = delta/(w b^3), C_V = V/sqrt(g b), C_R = R/(w b^3), C_M = M/(w b^4), C_d = d/b and the length/beam ratio L/b. Table I, p. 26, tabulates "Beam at main step". NACA Report 766, p. 7, also states step depth as a percentage "of the beam at the step". NACA ARR (Locke, March 1943), p. 3, uses the same b, "beam at the main step", and calls it the fundamental length characteristic of a seaplane hull.
measurement_convention.station: At the main step.

verification.rationale: Over the chines, excluding spray strips, agrees with ITTC's maximum breadth over chines for a hard-chine planing hull, B_PX (see maximum-beam), and makes this beam and maximum-beam comparable wherever a hull is widest at the step. entries.definition: The outboard upward curvature of the hull bottom near the chine, relative to the straight vee that would otherwise continue from the keel. Flare deflects spray outward and downward rather than up the hull side. Zero flare means a straight (unflared) vee bottom.

measurement_convention.datum: Relative to the unflared vee. Appendix B figure 1 shows both cases in transverse section: "Unflared Bottom" with a single straight vee where beta = beta_k, and "Flared Bottom" with the flare region marked and beta and beta_k shown as distinct angles.
measurement_convention.notes: Figure 3 shows the resulting pressure distributions for both cases: unflared runs P_k at keel falling linearly to 0.75 P_k at the chine; flared adds P_ch over the flared region.
measurement_convention.source: 14 CFR Part 25, Appendix B, figures 1 and 3
measurement_convention.station: Transverse, near the chine. May vary longitudinally; the regulation evaluates pressures at the "appropriate station".

entries.name: Chine flare angle

regulatory_mapping.caveats: C2 = 0.00213 applies to the UNFLARED bottom case, 25.533(b)(1). It is the correct constant only when chine flare is zero.

C3 = 0.0016 applies to the FLARED bottom case, 25.533(b)(2). A hull with non-zero chine flare must use the flared chine-pressure formula with C3, not the unflared formula with C2. C3 is absent from most secondary summaries of 25.533, so a tool built from a summary rather than the regulation will not have it at all.
Non-zero flare makes beta differ from beta_k. The keel pressure formula needs beta_k specifically; using an outboard or mean deadrise understates P_k because P_k varies as 1/tan(beta_k).

The 0.75 * P_k chine ratio is stated for the unflared bottom. For the flared case, 25.533(b)(2) gives the chine pressure its own formula and the distribution between chine and start-of-flare varies linearly.

verification.checked_against: 14 CFR 25.533(b)(1) and (b)(2) full text, eCFR issue 2026-07-07; Appendix B figures 1 and 3 read from the published images.
verification.notes: The `selects` relationship is the reason this layer is worth building. A units registry alone would confirm chine_flare is an angle in degrees and catch nothing else. The regulatory link is what makes "this hull is flared, so C3 applies" a statement a machine can check.

entries.bounds_rationale: cfr-25.533-b1-keel-pressure divides by tan(beta_k). Zero is singular. The upper figure is conceptual and must not be enforced as a rejection.
entries.definition: The transverse angle of the hull bottom measured AT THE KEEL. For an unflared bottom it equals the station deadrise; for a flared bottom it is the steeper of the pair, because the flare shallows the section outboard.

measurement_convention.datum: From the horizontal in a transverse section, taken at the keel itself rather than at any outboard point.
measurement_convention.notes: Appendix B figure 1 supplies no numeric values -- it fixes how the angle is measured and shows the unflared and flared cases side by side. beta_k is a design input, not a chart lookup.
measurement_convention.source: 14 CFR Part 25, Appendix B, figure 1 (image EC28SE91.055)
measurement_convention.station: Longitudinal position is wherever the pressure is being computed; the TRANSVERSE position is fixed at the keel. Both qualifiers are needed.

verification.checked_against: 14 CFR 25.533(b)(1) full text, eCFR issue 2026-07-07, and Appendix B figure 1 read from the published image.
verification.notes: Substituting a chine or mean deadrise here understates P_k, because P_k varies as 1/tan(beta_k) and beta_k is the steeper angle.

measurement_convention.datum: From the horizontal in a transverse section.
measurement_convention.notes: Also the station where the hull reference axis is tangent to the keel, per 25.527(b)(7), so it is doing double duty as a geometric datum.
measurement_convention.station: At the main step. Not "in the forebody" and not "at the CG" -- the takeoff condition names one station.

entries.bounds_rationale: Raised to the 2/3 power in the denominator of cfr-25.527-a1 and divided into by cfr-25.533-b2-flared-chine-pressure and cfr-25.533-c1-distributed-pressure. Zero is singular in all three, not merely unusual. The upper figure is conceptual and must NOT be enforced as a rejection.
entries.definition: The transverse angle between the hull bottom and the horizontal, at a given longitudinal station. It governs how sharply the vee parts the water and therefore how impact load is spread: a higher deadrise reduces peak water reaction and local bottom pressure at the cost of increased planing resistance and hump drag.

implementations.identifier: Dead rise at keel at main step
implementations.notes: All four tank models held at 20.0 deg. Reported at the keel at the main step, matching the beta_k convention exactly -- a useful cross-check that the convention here is the one the experimental literature uses.

measurement_convention.datum: Measured from the horizontal in a transverse section. For an UNFLARED bottom the angle is constant from keel to chine, so beta = beta_k. For a FLARED bottom the bottom curves near the chine: beta_k at the keel is the steeper angle, and beta at an outboard station is shallower.
measurement_convention.notes: Appendix B figure 1 is a pictorial nomenclature diagram, not a chart: it fixes how the angle is measured and shows the unflared/flared distinction. It supplies no numeric values. beta is a design input, not a value looked up from the regulation.
measurement_convention.source: 14 CFR Part 25, Appendix B, figure 1 (image EC28SE91.055)
measurement_convention.station: Longitudinal. 14 CFR 25.527(b)(4) requires the value "at the longitudinal station at which the load factor is being determined" -- it is not a single number for the hull.

entries.name: Deadrise angle at a longitudinal station

regulatory_mapping.caveats: Evaluated at the station where the load factor is being determined. For the step landing case of 25.527(a)(1) that is the main step.

The bow and stern landing cases evaluate at bow and stern stations, so the same formula is applied with DIFFERENT deadrise values. A model carrying one hull-wide deadrise cannot express this case correctly.

beta_k is deadrise AT THE KEEL specifically. Equal to beta only for an unflared bottom. Substituting a chine or mean deadrise into the keel pressure formula understates P_k, because P_k varies as 1/tan(beta_k).

verification.checked_against: 14 CFR 25.527(b)(4) and 25.533(b)(1) full text, eCFR issue 2026-07-07; Appendix B figure 1 read from the published image.
verification.notes: A TWO-VALUE fore/aft model is a DISCRETIZATION of a quantity the regulation treats as continuous along the hull. That is a reasonable modelling choice, but it is a choice, and it has a consequence: a warped forebody has deadrise varying WITHIN the forebody (NACA ARR 4F15 reports "forebody warping" of 1.2-2.1 deg per beam across its four models), so a single forebody constant cannot represent a warped hull faithfully. See deadrise-discretization-note below.

entries.bounds_rationale: cfr-25.535-b-deadrise-floor -- "need not be less than 15 degrees". The bound constrains the value USED IN THE FORMULA, not the shape the designer may draw. A consumer that rejects an 8 degree float has misread it.
entries.definition: Deadrise of an AUXILIARY float -- a wing-tip or sponson float -- at a station three-quarters of the distance from that float's bow to its step. A property of the float, not of the hull.

measurement_convention.datum: From the horizontal in a transverse section of the float.
measurement_convention.notes: Subject to a 15 degree floor, which is RELIEF and not a geometric limit: the float may physically have less, and the designer simply need not use the smaller value in the load formula. It is the regulation's own guard against the tan(beta) singularity, and the only one in Subpart C.
measurement_convention.station: Three-quarters of the distance from the float's own bow to the float's own step. Both the bow and the step are the float's, not the hull's.

entries.name: Auxiliary float dead rise at three-quarters bow-to-step

regulatory_mapping.caveats: The floor applies to the value substituted into the load formula, not to the geometry. A float with 8 degrees of deadrise is legal; the formula is simply evaluated at 15.

entries.name: Note: discretizing a station-dependent deadrise

regulatory_mapping.caveats: 25.527(a)(2) evaluates the load factor at bow and stern stations, each with its own beta and its own K1 from Appendix B figure 2. A model with constant forebody and afterbody deadrise supplies at most two distinct values where the regulation asks for a value per station. For a hull with significant forebody warp the bow deadrise is materially different from the mid-forebody value, and using the latter understates n_w at the bow -- the non-conservative direction.

aliases: draft of keel at main step
entries.definition: The vertical distance from the bottom of the keel at the main step down to the water line: how deep the hull sits at the step. Not a property of the hull alone. It depends on the load on the water, so a value means nothing without the load it was taken at.

measurement_convention.datum: The bottom of the keel at the main step. Sottorf: the "vertical distance of the water line from the bottom of the keel at the step".
measurement_convention.notes: Vertical, not normal to the keel or to the hull reference axis. Sottorf says so; the NACA reports do not repeat it. A value must carry its load. ARR 4F15 Figure 4 gives draft as a curve against C_delta, at rest, so a draft without the load and the at-rest condition is not reproducible. Underway, the draft at the step changes with speed and trim, and none of these definitions covers that case. Nondimensionalised as d/b, and which b is the report's: the beam at the main step in ARR 4F15, the maximum beam in Report 766. See beam-at-main-step and maximum-beam. This is the only flying-boat draft definition found. A block coefficient for a flying boat would need one; no source read builds a block coefficient from it.
measurement_convention.source: NACA TM 860 (Sottorf, April 1938), notation on the first page, symbol t_st; NACA ARR 4F15, p. 11, "d draft of keel at main step", with C_d = d/b, and Figure 4, "Static properties of the four models", which plots C_d against the load coefficient; NACA Report 766, p. 9, "d draft at main step", with C_d = d/b.
measurement_convention.station: At the main step.

entries.name: Hull draft at the main step

entries.bounds_rationale: Denominator of the forebody branch of cfr-25-appB-fig2-k1 and -k2.
entries.definition: Distance from the bow to the main step, measured parallel to the hull reference axis. The forebody is the planing surface that carries the hull at rest and through the hump; the step terminates it so that flow separates cleanly rather than sticking to the afterbody.

measurement_convention.datum: From the bow, parallel to the hull reference axis — the straight line in the plane of symmetry tangential to the keel at the main step, as fixed by 25.527(b)(7).
measurement_convention.notes: Because the endpoint is definitional, a tool carrying both a "step fraction" and a "forebody fraction" that are permitted to differ has two candidate values for L_f and no rule for choosing. A tool that carries both should say which one Appendix B reads.
measurement_convention.source: 14 CFR Part 25, Appendix B, figure 2 (image EC28SE91.056)
measurement_convention.station: Terminates AT THE MAIN STEP. This is definitional, not conventional: Appendix B figure 2 places x = L_f at the step and puts the K1 and K2 discontinuities there.

entries.name: Forebody length, bow to main step

verification.checked_against: 14 CFR 25.527(b)(7) full text and Appendix B figure 2, read from the published image, eCFR issue 2026-07-07.

entries.bounds_rationale: An area is not negative. Zero is inside the range on purpose: it is an aircraft with no horizontal tail, and nothing is singular there.
entries.definition: The area of the horizontal tail, stabilizer and elevator together, measured in the same manner as the wing area: with no deduction for the area blanketed by the body.

measurement_convention.datum: The plane of the tail's chords, as for the wing.
measurement_convention.notes: "Stabilizer and elevator together" is a reading: the report says the area is measured as the wing's is, the wing's includes its ailerons, and its "span" of a stabilizer is "inclusive of elevator". The report's rule speaks only of a stabilizer meeting a fuselage. It is silent on a horizontal tail carried by the fin.
measurement_convention.source: NACA Report No. 474, Nomenclature for Aeronautics, "area, measurement of (performance calculations): horizontal tail area"
measurement_convention.station: Whole surface. The blanketed area is "bounded within the fuselage by lateral straight lines that connect the intersections of the leading and trailing edges of the stabilizer with the sides of the fuselage, the fairings and fillets being ignored."

entries.name: Horizontal tail area

verification.checked_against: NACA Report No. 474 (reprint of 1939; originally published March 1934), the entry "area, measurement of", read from the NTRS scan, citation 20100021420.

entries.bounds_rationale: Every quantity stated as a fraction of hull length divides by it.
entries.definition: The length of the hull from its forepoint to its sternpost: the length of the hydrodynamic surfaces. Excludes any tail extension or fairing aft of the sternpost.

measurement_convention.datum: From the forepoint, the forward end of the hull. NACA TN 1570 names the same point the forward perpendicular (F.P.).
measurement_convention.line: DEFINED HERE: measured parallel to the hull reference axis, the straight line in the plane of symmetry tangent to the keel at the main step, as 14 CFR 25.527(b)(7) fixes it; the line forebody-length and afterbody-length are measured along. Not along a base line drawn elsewhere, and not horizontally at rest.
measurement_convention.notes: None of the three reports says along which line the length is measured: along the keel, along the hull reference axis, or horizontally. On a hull with a rising afterbody keel the three differ. ARR 4F15 Figure 7 draws two candidates 2 degrees apart, "TANGENT TO KEEL AT STEP", which is the hull reference axis, and a base line, with stations in inches aft of F.P. The line is therefore the ontology's choice; see verification.rationale. A READING, NOT A SOURCE'S TEXT: 14 CFR 25.529(a) measures the bow landing station from the bow to the step and the stern landing station from the step to the sternpost, so forebody-length plus afterbody-length spans this length. The regulation never states the sum. The length-beam ratio in every report read is this length over a beam, and which beam depends on the report; see beam-at-main-step. NOT Locke's L. NACA ARR (Locke, March 1943) forms its over-all length coefficient L/b by adding its forebody and afterbody equations (p. 5), and ends the afterbody at "the second step or stern post, whichever is shorter" (p. 3). On a hull with a second step that is shorter than this length, and the report never defines L on its own.
measurement_convention.source: NACA ARR 4F15, p. 11 (symbol L) and Table I, p. 26; NACA TN 1570, p. 3 (symbol L); NACA ARR L5G23, Table I, p. 11.
measurement_convention.station: To the sternpost (S.P.), the aft end of the afterbody planing bottom. NOT the over-all length. ARR L5G23 Table I tabulates the two as separate rows, and for its NACA series they differ by the tail extension: 114.85 against 83.33 inches for model 144.

entries.name: Hull length, forepoint to sternpost

verification.checked_against: Read from the NTRS scans, page images and not only the text layer: NACA ARR 4F15 (Davidson and Locke, June 1944), citation 19930093044, PDF sha256 fdbb07cd2b81...a8f5, pp. 11 and 26 and Figure 7; NACA TN 1570 (Carter and Haar, April 1948), citation 19930082382, sha256 2a1555ccebf7...957f, p. 3; NACA ARR L5G23 (Land, Bidwell and Goldenbaum, October 1945), citation 19930093020, sha256 c3cb5500945f...1db8, Table I, p. 11; NACA ARR (Locke, March 1943), citation 19930093017. All fetched 2026-09-23. The bounded search for the measuring line (docs/CONOPS.md) ended with these: none states it.
verification.notes: The endpoints are the sources': the reports read agree on forepoint (or F.P.) to sternpost, and ARR L5G23 applies it across the DVL, NACA and Stevens series alike. The line is the ontology's choice of the regulation's axis. A value from a report measured along another line differs by the cosine of the angle between them: 0.06 percent at ARR 4F15's 2 degrees.
verification.rationale: forebody-length and afterbody-length, which run bow to step and step to sternpost, are measured parallel to the hull reference axis, so this length is their sum exactly when it is taken along the same line. The axis is the regulation's own (25.527(b)(7)) and already in the corpus, and it is a property of the hull's lines alone: a horizontal length at rest would depend on load and trim, as draft does. Read by every length-beam ratio. Chosen by the designer, 2026-09-23. It corrects the base line first chosen the same day, which ran 2 degrees off the line its two parts use (#23).

entries.bounds_rationale: Denominator of every Langley-series coefficient, as b^3 in the load and resistance coefficients.
entries.definition: The greatest beam of the hull, wherever along it that occurs. The characteristic dimension of the Langley tank tests: NACA Report 766 says the maximum beam "was chosen as the characteristic dimension".

measurement_convention.datum: Transverse, over the chines, excluding spray strips: DEFINED HERE. The NACA sources do not say whether the beam is taken over the chines, over spray strips, or over the flare. ITTC, for a hard-chine planing hull, defines a maximum breadth over chines, B_PX, "excluding external spray strips", and this entry agrees with it; whether Langley measured the same way is not stated.
measurement_convention.notes: Bare "beam" is not an alias of this entry or of beam-at-main-step. It is used for both, and a tool that writes it has not said which.
measurement_convention.source: NACA Report 766, p. 9: "b maximum beam, feet", in C_delta = delta/(w b^3) and the other coefficients; p. 7 for station 10. NACA TN 1570, p. 3: "b maximum beam of hull, feet". ITTC Symbols and Terminology List, Version 2024, section 3.1.1, for B_PX.
measurement_convention.station: The station of greatest beam, which need not be the step. On Report 766's model 84 it is station 10, "maximum beam", while step depth is stated against the beam at the step.

entries.name: Hull maximum beam

verification.checked_against: NACA Report 766 (Parkinson, Olson, Draley and Luoma, 1943), NTRS citation 19930091845, PDF sha256 bfd856295b36...4598, pp. 7 and 9; NACA TN 1570 (April 1948), citation 19930082382, sha256 2a1555ccebf7...957f, p. 3; ITTC Symbols and Terminology List, Version 2024, PDF sha256 5eb1eb88af50...77ee, section 3.1.1. All read from the page images or the publisher's PDF, fetched 2026-09-23.
verification.notes: The station is Langley's; the convention is the ontology's and agrees with ITTC's. A Langley value is not thereby claimed to have been measured over the chines.
verification.rationale: The Langley definition gives the station; what the beam is taken over it leaves open. Over the chines, excluding spray strips, is the convention of ITTC's B_PX, the one public standard read that states one for a hard-chine planing hull, and the same one beam-at-main-step uses, so the two beams differ only in station. Read by every Langley-series coefficient. Chosen by the designer, 2026-09-23.

entries.definition: Ratio of the distance, measured parallel to the hull reference axis, from the centre of gravity to the hull longitudinal station being computed, to the pitch radius of gyration of the seaplane.

measurement_convention.datum: From the CG, parallel to the hull reference axis — the straight line in the plane of symmetry tangential to the keel at the main step.
measurement_convention.notes: Measured FROM THE CG, so cfr-25.523-b-critical-cg makes this a swept quantity: moving the CG within the certified envelope changes it at every station simultaneously.
measurement_convention.station: Per station. Zero at the CG station and growing toward bow and stern, which is what makes the bow and stern cases of 25.527(a)(2) milder than the raw K1 values alone suggest.

entries.name: Station-to-CG distance over pitch radius of gyration

regulatory_mapping.caveats: 25.523(b) does not name r_x. It requires critical CG positions to be considered, and r_x is measured from the CG, so the requirement propagates into this parameter as a sweep rather than a value.

verification.checked_against: 14 CFR 25.527(b)(7) full text, eCFR issue 2026-07-07.

entries.definition: Ratio of the lateral distance between the centre of gravity and the plane of symmetry of an AUXILIARY FLOAT, to the radius of gyration in roll.

measurement_convention.datum: Lateral, from the CG to the float's plane of symmetry.
measurement_convention.notes: The lateral analogue of r_x, and a plausible thing to substitute r_x into. Both appear as (1 + r^2)^(2/3) in their respective denominators, so the substitution yields a believable number rather than an obvious error.
measurement_convention.station: n/a

entries.name: Float lateral offset over roll radius of gyration

verification.checked_against: 14 CFR 25.535(b) full text, eCFR issue 2026-07-07.

entries.definition: Forebody length as used by spray and planing correlations. A hydrodynamic correlation length, chosen to fit experimental spray data, which need not coincide with the regulatory step station.

measurement_convention.datum: From the bow.
measurement_convention.notes: Declared so that the distinction from forebody-length is nameable and the conflation is checkable. It is legitimate for a tool to carry both.
measurement_convention.source: Not a regulatory quantity. The forebody length of Parkinson-type spray correlations.
measurement_convention.station: Set by whichever correlation is in use, not by the main step. This is the whole point of the separate entry.

entries.name: Hydrodynamic spray forebody length

regulatory_mapping.caveats: NOT interchangeable with L_f. This mapping records what the quantity is wrongly substituted INTO, not what it legitimately feeds. Appendix B needs the step station; supplying a spray length instead relocates the K1 and K2 discontinuity away from the physical step. No constraint in this corpus consumes this parameter.

verification.checked_against: Not a regulatory quantity and not stated in 14 CFR. Recorded because it shares a name with the step station, forebody-length, and substituting one for the other moves the Appendix B discontinuity.

entries.definition: Seaplane stalling speed with flaps extended in the appropriate LANDING position and with no slipstream effect.

measurement_convention.datum: No slipstream effect — power off. The regulation says so explicitly, and it matters for a high-wing flying boat with propellers well above the wing.
measurement_convention.notes: § 25.533 uses BOTH stalling speeds in adjacent paragraphs: the local pressures of (b) take V_S1, the distributed pressures of (c) take V_S0. Substituting one for the other changes the result by the square of the speed ratio. This is the detail a summarizer drops.
measurement_convention.station: n/a

entries.name: Stalling speed, landing flaps, no slipstream

regulatory_mapping.caveats: UNIT UNRESOLVED in that constraint. § 25.535(f) is the only water load formula written in genuine physical quantities, so its dimensions must close on their own and only do so with the speed in ft/s, while the glossary says knots. A factor of 2.85. Do not bind this parameter to that constraint until the question is settled.

verification.checked_against: 14 CFR 25.527(b)(3) and 25.533(c)(1) full text, eCFR issue 2026-07-07.

entries.definition: Seaplane stalling speed at the design water takeoff weight with flaps extended in the appropriate TAKEOFF position.

measurement_convention.datum: At the design water takeoff weight — a different weight from V_S0's.
measurement_convention.notes: Two things differ from V_S0 at once: the flap position and the weight the speed is evaluated at. A tool carrying a single stall speed cannot express either difference.
measurement_convention.station: n/a

entries.name: Stalling speed at design water takeoff weight, takeoff flaps

verification.checked_against: 14 CFR 25.533(b)(1) and 25.531(b) full text, eCFR issue 2026-07-07.

entries.bounds_rationale: A station of the hull lies between its forepoint and its sternpost. A station forward of the forepoint is not a station of the hull. Reported, not enforced.
entries.definition: Where a transverse station of the hull lies along it: the distance from the hull's forepoint to the station's plane, measured parallel to the hull reference axis, positive aft. A hull's lines are drawn as sections at stations, and an offsets table is indexed by them.

measurement_convention.datum: From the forepoint, the forward end of the hull, the same point hull-length and forebody-length are measured from. NACA ARR 4F15 names it the forepoint and the forward perpendicular (F.P.).
measurement_convention.line: DEFINED HERE: measured parallel to the hull reference axis, the straight line in the plane of symmetry tangent to the keel at the main step, as 14 CFR 25.527(b)(7) fixes it. Not along a base line.
measurement_convention.notes: ARR 4F15 draws its stations square to a base line, which its Figure 7 shows 2 degrees from the tangent to the keel at the step. The ontology measures along the hull reference axis instead, as it does hull-length, so that a station at the step is exactly forebody-length aft of the forepoint and one at the sternpost exactly hull-length. A position read from such a drawing along its base line differs by the cosine of the angle between the lines: 0.06 percent at 2 degrees. A drawing whose longitudinal coordinate has its origin elsewhere, at a datum ahead of the bow for instance, gives a coordinate and not this quantity. The station position is that coordinate less the forepoint's.
measurement_convention.source: NACA ARR 4F15, Figure 6 ("station nos. are inches aft of forepoint") and Figure 7 ("ins. aft of F.P.").
measurement_convention.station: To the plane of the station: a plane normal to the hull reference axis. A station at the forepoint is at zero; one at the main step is at forebody-length; one at the sternpost is at hull-length.

entries.name: Station position, aft of the forepoint

verification.checked_against: The bounded search (docs/CONOPS.md). Read from the NTRS scans, page images: NACA ARR 4F15 (Davidson and Locke, June 1944), citation 19930093044, PDF sha256 fdbb07cd2b81...a8f5, Figures 6 and 7 (PDF pages 32 and 33). One search of NTRS, "flying-boat hull lines stations", found NACA TN 491 (Shoemaker and Parkinson, February 1934), citation 19930081479, sha256 ab8a5d0db7f0...2215, read whole: it derives its length series by "uniformly increasing the distance between stations" (p. 4) and numbers no station. Fetched 2026-09-26.
verification.rationale: The sources read agree on the origin, the forepoint, and state no line but their base line. The line is the ontology's choice of the regulation's axis, the one hull-length, forebody-length and afterbody-length are measured along, so that the positions of the forepoint, the step and the sternpost are those lengths exactly. Read by a design tool that records the position at which a station was inserted into an offsets table, and by any exchange of offsets tables between tools. Chosen by the designer, 2026-09-26.

entries.bounds_rationale: An area is not negative. Zero is inside the range on purpose: it is an aircraft with no vertical tail, and nothing is singular there.
entries.definition: The area of the actual outline of the rudder and the fin, projected in the vertical plane, the fairings and fillets being ignored.

measurement_convention.datum: The vertical plane. For a single centreline fin, the plane of symmetry.
measurement_convention.notes: The asymmetry with horizontal-tail-area is the reason the two are separate entries and not one "tail area" with a direction. Report 474 does not say whether a dorsal fin is part of the fin, nor how twin fins are summed; both are the ontology's, above.
measurement_convention.source: NACA Report No. 474, Nomenclature for Aeronautics, "area, measurement of (performance calculations): vertical tail area"
measurement_convention.station: The ACTUAL OUTLINE. Unlike the wing and the horizontal tail, nothing is extended through the body: the area stops where the fin does. DEFINED HERE: every vertical fin of the aircraft, with its rudder, summed; twin or multiple fins add. A dorsal fin is excluded, as a fairing or fillet is.

entries.name: Vertical tail area

verification.checked_against: NACA Report No. 474 (reprint of 1939; originally published March 1934), the entry "area, measurement of", read from the NTRS scan, citation 20100021420. It is silent on dorsal fins and on twin fins; the bounded search ended there.
verification.rationale: Summing the fins makes the area the aircraft's directional surface whatever the arrangement, which is what a tail volume coefficient reads. Excluding the dorsal fin follows Report 474's own rule that fairings and fillets are ignored, and keeps the area to the fin's actual outline. Chosen by the designer, 2026-09-23.

entries.bounds_rationale: Aspect ratio, mean chord and every aerodynamic coefficient divide by it.
entries.definition: The area of the projection of the wing's actual outline on the plane of the chords, with no deduction for the part blanketed by the fuselage or nacelles, and including the ailerons.

measurement_convention.datum: The plane of the chords. The area is of the projection on that plane, not the developed surface, so dihedral does not enter.
measurement_convention.notes: The whole projected area, through the body. An area that deducts the blanketed part, or that replaces the actual outline with another, is not this quantity, whatever symbol a tool gives it. A READING, NOT THE REPORT'S TEXT: on a flying boat the hull is taken as the fuselage, so the wing runs through the hull. The report says "fuselage or nacelles" and does not repeat the rule for a hull; see verification.notes.
measurement_convention.source: NACA Report No. 474, Nomenclature for Aeronautics, "area, measurement of (performance calculations): wing area"
measurement_convention.station: Whole wing, tip to tip. "For the purpose of calculating area, a wing is considered to extend without interruption through the fuselage and nacelles." The part inside the body is bounded by two lateral straight lines joining the points where the leading and trailing edges meet the body, "ignoring fairings and fillets".

entries.name: Wing area

verification.checked_against: NACA Report No. 474 (reprint of 1939; originally published March 1934), the entry "area, measurement of", read from the NTRS scan, citation 20100021420 (PDF sha256 e900d8023594...4626 as fetched 2026-09-18).
verification.notes: Report 474 writes "fuselage or nacelles". "Hull" is this entry's extension to a flying boat, which the report defines as "a form of seaplane whose main body or hull provides flotation"; it does not repeat the area rule for a hull, and the extension is a reading, not its text.

entries.bounds_rationale: A ratio of two positive quantities.
entries.definition: The ratio of the span to the mean chord of the wing; that is, the ratio of the square of the span to the wing area. The mean chord is the wing area divided by the span.

measurement_convention.datum: Derived, never measured: wing-span squared over wing-area. It inherits both conventions, so it is the gross area, through the body, and the projected span.
measurement_convention.notes: Of wing-area, wing-span and this, any two determine the third. A tool that stores all three as independent values can hold a wing that does not exist. Report 474 separately defines an "effective aspect ratio", by equal induced drag with an elliptical wing; that is an aerodynamic result and is not this quantity.
measurement_convention.source: NACA Report No. 474, Nomenclature for Aeronautics, "aspect ratio" and "chord, mean, of a wing"
measurement_convention.station: Whole wing.

entries.name: Wing aspect ratio

verification.checked_against: NACA Report No. 474 (reprint of 1939; originally published March 1934), the entries "aspect ratio" and "chord, mean, of a wing", read from the NTRS scan, citation 20100021420.

entries.bounds_rationale: Mean chord divides the wing area by it.
entries.definition: The maximum distance, measured parallel to the lateral axis, from tip to tip of the wing, inclusive of ailerons.

measurement_convention.datum: Parallel to the lateral axis of the aircraft.
measurement_convention.notes: Report 474 also defines an "effective span", the true span less a correction for tip loss, which is an aerodynamic quantity and not this one. It says nothing of tip-mounted floats or tip devices: whether a tool's span includes them is a convention the tool must state.
measurement_convention.source: NACA Report No. 474, Nomenclature for Aeronautics, "span"
measurement_convention.station: Tip to tip: the maximum such distance. Projected, so a wing with dihedral has a span shorter than the length measured along its surface.

entries.name: Wing span

verification.checked_against: NACA Report No. 474 (reprint of 1939; originally published March 1934), the entry "span", read from the NTRS scan, citation 20100021420.
